En 1869, il range les éléments dans un t: In 1869, he arranged the elements in a table and left empty squares in it for elements not yet known, whose properties he predicted. Gallium and germanium arrived a few years later. He only cut his hair once a year.
Né esclave dans le Missouri, il devient: Born a slave in Missouri, he became a botanist and chemist at the Tuskegee Institute. He taught farmers to alternate cotton, which exhausts the soil, with peanuts, which enrich it with nitrogen, and looked for hundreds of uses for these plants. Contrary to legend, he did not invent peanut butter.
Physicienne autrichienne, elle fuit l'Al: An Austrian physicist, she fled Nazi Germany in 1938. A few months later, with her nephew Otto Frisch, she explained the results of her former colleague Otto Hahn: the uranium nucleus had split in two, it was fission. The Nobel went to Hahn alone. Element 109 bears her name.
Biologiste marine, elle publie en 1962 P: A marine biologist, in 1962 she published Silent Spring, about the damage done by pesticides like DDT. The chemical industry called her a “fanatic.” A presidential science committee largely backed her in 1963, and agricultural DDT was banned in the United States in 1972. She died of cancer two years after the book.
Il invente l'électronégativité en 1932 e: He invented electronegativity in 1932 and published The Nature of the Chemical Bond in 1939. Two unshared Nobel Prizes, chemistry and peace. He also got things spectacularly wrong: he proposed a triple helix for DNA, and believed high doses of vitamin C prevented colds.
Sa thèse de 1884 sur les ions en solutio: His 1884 thesis on ions in solution, which defined acids and bases, received the lowest grade that still allowed it to pass. It earned him the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1903. In 1896, he also calculated that doubling the CO₂ in the air would warm the Earth by several degrees.
En 1908 à Leyde, il liquéfie l'hélium à: In 1908 in Leiden, he liquefied helium at four degrees above absolute zero. Three years later, he discovered that mercury, just as cold, loses all electrical resistance: superconductivity. His laboratory's motto: “Door meten tot weten,” through measurement to knowledge.
